newsitem.title: GERMANY: German forwarders protest at proposed ban on rate.
newsitem.headline: German forwarders protest at proposed ban on rate.

text.p: German freight forwarders have protested at German government plans to end their right to issue recommended prices for overland transport.
The freight forwarders association BSL said the economics ministry had proposed to scrap the industry's exemption from a ban on pricing cartels.
An end to the exemption of the association's recommendations would have a dramatic effect on the forwarding industry, the BSL's newly-formed overland transport committee said in a statement.

"The BSL price recommendations are not anti-competitive, as the economics minister says, but are a calculation basis for groupage freight which is also recognised by freight shippers," the statement said.
The BSL has issued recommended prices twice a year for overland groupage transport since the liberalisation of the transport market in 1994.
The recommendations go to industry associations for comment and to the German cartel office for approval before they can go into force, observers noted.
The last round of recommended price rises was in February when rates hikes of 1.9-2.5 percent were suggested by the association to freight forwarders.
The BSL also repeated its protest at a bill to reform German transport law which could increase insurance liability for freight forwarders by up to 250 percent.
A justice ministry bill in May did not take sufficient account of the differences between road hauliers and freight forwarders and their corresponding level of risk, the statement said.
Higher insurance premiums could have major financial consequences for forwarders and the new premium levels should be fixed to reflect the interests of forwarders and freight shippers, it added.

The BSL first warned last December that an increase in maximum liability to 17.90 marks per kg from five marks per kg could cost the industry 500 million marks in higher premiums. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom. Tel +44 171 542 7706 Fax+5017
